title: Routing Score Workbench
description: A Chart.js horizontal bar chart workbench for the MicroSim routing rubric. For each of ten objectives the learner scores three or four candidate types with sliders over the five shaded rubric bands, reads the routing-criteria guideline for each band on hover, answers a clarifying-question prompt when the top two scores are within 10 points, and reveals author-written reference bands with a count of scores that fall inside them.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Educational Technology
Instructional Design
MicroSim Engineering
Rubrics

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
learningObjectives: The learner will justify a type choice by assigning rubric scores to competing types for a described objective and explaining any routing ambiguity.
prerequisites: Keyword routing and the routing decision tree
Classifying an objective by Bloom level and verb

customPlugins: rubricBands: shaded bands and band labels (beforeDatasetsDraw); reference-band boxes and value labels (afterDatasetsDraw)

accessibility.notes: Sliders are native HTML range inputs with aria-labels; all feedback is plain HTML text.

controls.label: Reveal reference bands
controls.action: Overlay the reference band for each candidate and count scores inside it

controls.label: Next objective
controls.action: Load the next of ten objectives and reset the sliders to 50

controls.label: Show ambiguity warning
controls.action: Show the clarifying-question banner when the top two scores are within 10 points

controls.label: Clarifying questions
controls.action: Choose one of two questions; feedback says whether it separates the candidates

equations: band = 90-100 perfect, 70-89 strong, 50-69 moderate, 30-49 weak, 0-29 poor
ambiguous when top score - second score <= 10
assumptions: Band guidelines are taken from the generator skill's routing-criteria.md; reference bands are teaching examples written for this bank.
limitations: The ten-point ambiguity margin is this book's suggestion, not part of the skill.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judgment with explicit criteria, followed by calibration against reference bands
keyQuestions: Which rubric guideline describes this objective for each candidate?
How far ahead must the top candidate be before you commit?
Which single question would separate two close candidates?
commonMisconceptions: Routing scores are computed by a formula.
The highest score always wins, even by five points.
assessmentOpportunities: Share of scores inside the reference band
Choice of clarifying question on ambiguous objectives
Written justification of the top score
